chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Ismail ibn Bazie, from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl, from Abu al-Subah al-Kinani, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the pregnant woman is one (divorce), and her waiting period is the closest of the two terms.
ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period for a pregnant woman who is divorced according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of talaq al-hamil, establishing that a single pronouncement suffices for validity and defining the iddah as the period until childbirth, which is the primary marker. The phrase 'aqarr al-ajalain' (the nearer of the two periods) reflects the scholarly consensus that the completion of gestation supersedes the standard three-month waiting period for non-pregnant women, ensuring the child's lineage is clear. This ruling is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining the end of the waiting period and the mother's eligibility for remarriage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Muhammad Bin Ismail Bin Bazie, from Muhammad Bin Al Fuzayl, from Abu Al Sabbah Al Kinani, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘A divorce of the pregnant woman is once, and her waiting period is the closest of the two terms (three menstruations or the childbirth)’.
en.sarwar: 2. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il ibn Bazi‘ from Muhammad ibn al-Fudayl from abu al- Sabbah al-Kinaniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Divorce of a pregnant woman is once and her waiting period is the closest of the two periods, (that is, childbirth or three months).’”
